correctness.rationale: A reconstructed four-step argument gives the uniform necessary logarithmic proximity O(max(q,r^-1)^m), then a polynomial lower bound on nonzero algebraic logarithmic forms enforces t>=exp(cm). For sufficiency, the same Baker bound supplies ||j h log_b r||>>j^-D; Erdős–Turán yields uniform discrepancy O(Q^(D/(D+1))) and an interval hit within Q=O(r^((D+1)m)) steps. An even k if alpha<0 preserves sign. The nondominant term divided by b^t is O((qr)^m q^Q)<1/3, so an integer appended block exists with t<=exp(Cm). Finite exact-integer tests in the included script agree, but are not relied upon as infinite proof.
